goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — The mutation never rejects cancelled or rejected bookings, so an attendee can use an inactive booking to send arbitrary recipients CONFIRMED calendar invitations.

adjudication.rationale: The addGuests.handler.ts code fetches a booking by ID and checks if the user is a team admin/owner, organizer, or attendee, but it never checks the booking's status field. Looking at the diff, there's no validation that booking.status is in an active state (like ACCEPTED or PENDING). This means a cancelled or rejected booking could still be used to add guests and send calendar invitations with CONFIRMED status, as shown in the email templates that set status: 'CONFIRMED'. This is a legitimate security/correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — Requiring both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner denies legitimate team admins despite the advertised admin-or-owner authorization.
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - that the code incorrectly requires BOTH isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true (using &&), when it should allow either one (using ||). The candidate correctly points out this denies legitimate team admins, which is the same logical error described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The unbounded guest array lets any authorized attendee amplify one request into arbitrarily many database rows, calendar invitees, and outbound emails.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZAddGuestsInputSchema at line 5 defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no maximum length constraint. The handler in addGuests.handler.ts processes all guests by creating database rows (prisma.booking.update with createMany), updating calendar attendees (eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees), and sending emails (sendAddGuestsEmails). An authorized user (attendee, organizer, or team admin) could submit thousands of guest emails in a single request, causing resource exhaustion. This is a real security/DoS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Filtering only against the preexisting attendee list does not deduplicate the request itself, so repeated addresses create duplicate attendee rows and notifications.
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the uniqueGuests filtering only checks against existing attendees but doesn't deduplicate within the input request itself, which can lead to duplicate attendee rows being created when the client submits repeated emails. Both comments point to the same bug in the same file, just with slightly different wording.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Case-sensitive guest comparisons allow case variants to bypass both the lowercased blacklist and existing-attendee exclusion.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Concurrent additions can each publish a different attendee snapshot, allowing the last external-calendar update to overwrite guests committed by the other request.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition in the addGuests.handler.ts. Looking at lines 85-100, the handler reads attendees, adds new guests via prisma.booking.update with createMany, then calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees with the updated attendee list. If two concurrent requests execute this flow, each will read the current attendees, add their guests, and push to the external calendar. The second request's calendar update could overwrite the first's changes since there's no locking or atomic read-modify-write pattern. This is a legitimate concurrency bug that could cause data loss in external calendar systems.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — Calendar synchronization uses the caller's credentials rather than the booking organizer's, so authorized attendee or team-admin calls cannot reliably update the organizer's event.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, line 158 shows `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` where ctx.user is the caller (the person making the API request). Then at line 160-163, these credentials are used to create an EventManager that calls `updateCalendarAttendees`. However, the booking may belong to a different organizer (booking.userId), and the caller could be an attendee or team admin who has permission to add guests but doesn't have the organizer's calendar credentials. This means the calendar update would fail or update the wrong calendar when a non-organizer adds guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — Because attendee rows are committed before calendar synchronization, a calendar failure returns an error while leaving guests persisted and a retry unable to reconcile them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in addGuests.handler.ts that guests are first persisted to the database via prisma.booking.update (lines 87-101), then calendar synchronization happens via eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees (line 165), and finally emails are sent. If updateCalendarAttendees fails, the function throws an error but the guests are already committed to the database. On retry, the uniqueGuests filter (lines 68-72) will exclude these already-added guests, making reconciliation impossible. This is a real transactional consistency bug where partial state can be left in the database.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Passing the original input instead of uniqueGuests misclassifies any already-present address in a mixed request as newly invited and resends its initial booking email.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169 — Swallowing sendAddGuestsEmails failures reports success even when only a subset of organizer and attendee notifications was delivered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 168-172 in addGuests.handler.ts that sendAddGuestsEmails errors are caught and only logged ('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'), then the function returns success ('Guests added'). This is a real concern - if email sending fails (partially or fully), the user gets a success response. However, this is a design/architecture concern rather than a bug, as the guests ARE actually added to the database before the email step. The pattern of not failing the entire operation due to email failures is common, but the finding correctly identifies that this could lead to misleading success messages when notifications weren't delivered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — The constructed CalendarEvent omits team members, so sendAddGuestsEmails silently skips its team-member notification branch.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in addGuests.handler.ts the CalendarEvent 'evt' object is constructed without a 'team' property (lines 117-143). In email-manager.ts, sendAddGuestsEmails checks 'if (calendarEvent.team?.members)' to send team member notifications (lines 530-534). Since 'evt' has no 'team' property, this condition will always be false, meaning team members will never receive the add guests notification email even though the code path exists for it. This is a real bug where the handler doesn't populate the team data needed by the email function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The public mutation accepts duplicate guest addresses even though only the bundled UI rejects them, allowing non-UI callers to create duplicate attendees.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff, the schema in addGuests.schema.ts (line 5) only validates that guests is an array of email strings with no duplicate check. The duplicate validation exists only in the UI component AddGuestsDialog.tsx (lines 25-28) using ZAddGuestsInputSchema with a .refine() check. However, the server-side handler in addGuests.handler.ts does filter duplicates against existing attendees (lines 68-72 with uniqueGuests), but it doesn't reject the request if the input array itself contains duplicates - it would just process them. The handler throws an error only if uniqueGuests.length === 0, meaning all provided emails were already attendees. If a caller sends ['a@b.com', 'a@b.com'] and neither is an existing attendee, both would pass the uniqueGuests filter and potentially create duplicate attendees. This is a real bug where API callers bypassing the UI could create duplicate attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — Requiring both isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner rejects users who have either permitted team role instead of accepting either role.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 47-48 in addGuests.handler.ts: `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));` - This uses `&&` (AND) operator, meaning a user must be BOTH team admin AND team owner to pass this check. The variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` suggests the intent was to accept users with EITHER role, which would require `||` (OR) operator. This is a logic bug that would incorrectly reject team admins who aren't owners and team owners who aren't admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Only blacklist entries are lowercased, so mixed-case guest input bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same security vulnerability as the golden comment: the blacklist check only lowercases the blacklist entries but not the input guest emails, allowing bypass of BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS by using mixed-case email input. Both point to the same file (addGuests.handler.ts) and the same underlying bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Case-sensitive attendee authorization rejects a legitimate attendee when session and stored email casing differ.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a case-sensitivity issue at line 52 in addGuests.handler.ts. The code uses `booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)` which performs a case-sensitive comparison. Email addresses are case-insensitive by RFC standards, so if a user registered with 'User@Example.com' but the booking stored 'user@example.com', the authorization check would fail even though they are the same person. This is a real bug that could deny legitimate attendees the ability to add guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Filtering only against existing attendees does not deduplicate the submitted array, so repeated emails create duplicate attendee rows.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts lines 72-76, the uniqueGuests filter only checks against existing booking.attendees to avoid duplicates with already-registered attendees. However, if the input 'guests' array itself contains duplicate emails (e.g., ['a@b.com', 'a@b.com']), the filter does not deduplicate within the submitted array. The schema validation in addGuests.schema.ts only validates that each element is an email, not that they are unique. The client-side validation in AddGuestsDialog.tsx does check for uniqueness with ZAddGuestsInputSchema, but this is client-side only and can be bypassed. The server-side handler would then create duplicate attendee rows for the same email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Case-sensitive existing-attendee comparison inserts a duplicate when the same email is submitted with different casing.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 76 in addGuests.handler.ts, the code filters unique guests with: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. This is a case-sensitive string comparison. If an existing attendee has email 'User@Example.com' and someone tries to add 'user@example.com', the comparison would return false (they're not equal case-sensitively), allowing a duplicate email to be inserted. Email addresses should be compared case-insensitively since email local parts are typically case-insensitive in practice. This is a real bug that could lead to duplicate attendees.

Both are about the sendAddGuestsEmails function incorrectly handling the classification of attendees when determining who receives which type of email. The golden comment explains that the function passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array but checks against newGuests (the input guests array), which causes misclassification. The candidate issue describes the same problem - that passing the original guests array causes existing attendees to be misclassified as new and receive the wrong emails. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — Building EventManager with the requester's credentials prevents attendee or team-admin actions from updating the organizer's calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the addGuests.handler.ts. At line 158, the code gets credentials using `ctx.user` (the requester) via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, and then creates EventManager with those credentials. However, the handler allows attendees and team admins (not just the organizer) to add guests (lines 46-51 check isTeamAdminOrOwner, isOrganizer, or isAttendee). When an attendee or team admin adds guests, the EventManager will use their credentials instead of the organizer's credentials, which means `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` at line 165 will fail to update the organizer's calendar since it doesn't have the organizer's calendar credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — Discarding the calendar-update outcome lets the mutation report success when provider updates silently fail.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 165 in addGuests.handler.ts, the code calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` but does not check or handle its return value. If the calendar update fails silently (returns an error result without throwing), the mutation continues and reports success via `return { message: "Guests added" }`. This is a valid concern about incomplete error handling for a new feature, but it's not strictly a bug since the database update succeeded - it's more of a robustness/completeness issue. The finding correctly identifies that calendar provider failures could go unnoticed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Swallowing sendAddGuestsEmails failures returns success even when no guest-change notifications were delivered.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 168-171 in addGuests.handler.ts that sendAddGuestsEmails errors are caught and only logged ('Error sending AddGuestsEmails'), then the function returns success ('Guests added'). This is a real concern - the guests are added to the database but if email notifications fail, the API returns success without indicating the notification failure. However, this is a design choice rather than a bug - the core operation (adding guests) succeeded. Similar patterns exist in other parts of the codebase for email sending. It's an important architectural concern about silent failures but not strictly a bug since the primary operation completed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — The constructed CalendarEvent never sets team members, making sendAddGuestsEmails' team-notification branch unreachable.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, the CalendarEvent 'evt' object constructed at lines 108-131 does not include a 'team' property with 'members'. In sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts lines 522-543), there's a branch that checks 'if (calendarEvent.team?.members)' to send emails to team members. Since 'evt' never sets 'team.members', this branch will never execute, meaning team members won't receive notification emails when guests are added. This is a real bug where the team notification functionality is broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:529 — Guest-change emails ignore disableStandardEmails flags and notify hosts and attendees whose event type suppresses those messages.
matched_golden_ids: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the sendAddGuestsEmails function (or guest-change emails) does not check/ignores the disableStandardEmails flags, which could result in sending emails when they should be suppressed. The candidate even specifies the file location (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:529) and describes the same consequence - notifying hosts and attendees when the event type has those messages disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:32 — Initializing the guest list with an empty-string sentinel makes an untouched dialog enter the invalid-email state instead of representing no guests.
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: initializing the guest list with an empty string (['']) instead of an empty array ([]). The golden comment mentions this 'may cause validation issues' while the candidate specifically describes the consequence as 'makes an untouched dialog enter the invalid-email state'. Both suggest the same underlying problem - the empty string sentinel/initial value causes validation problems - and both imply the solution is to start with an empty array instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — Interpolating an optional error code always creates a truthy string, so the unable-to-add fallback can never be shown.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 43 in AddGuestsDialog.tsx: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`;` - When err.data?.code is undefined, the template literal produces 'undefined: <translated message>', which is always a truthy string. Therefore, the fallback `t('unable_to_add_guests')` in `showToast(message || t('unable_to_add_guests'), 'error')` will never be used because `message` is always truthy (even when code is undefined, it becomes the string 'undefined: ...'). This is a real bug in the error handling logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 — The dialog duplicates the procedure's email schema and the copies already disagree on whether duplicate addresses are valid

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different schemas for validating guest emails. In AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26, ZAddGuestsInputSchema uses z.array(z.string().email()).refine() to check that emails are unique (uniqueEmails.size === emails.length). However, in addGuests.schema.ts, the schema is simply z.array(z.string().email()) without any uniqueness check. This means the client-side validation rejects duplicates while the server-side schema accepts them. This is a real inconsistency that could cause confusing behavior - the UI might show an error for duplicates, but if bypassed, the server would accept them. The finding correctly identifies that the schemas disagree.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 — This leaf module imports its own package barrel, creating a circular dependency through the new MultiEmail export and coupling it to the aggregate UI entry point

adjudication.rationale: Looking at packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx line 2, it imports from '@calcom/ui' which is the barrel export of the same package. Looking at packages/ui/index.tsx, the diff shows 'export { default as MultiEmail } from "./form/MultiEmailLazy"' is being added. MultiEmailLazy imports MultiEmail.tsx dynamically. So the chain is: MultiEmail.tsx imports from @calcom/ui (barrel) -> barrel exports MultiEmail from MultiEmailLazy -> MultiEmailLazy imports MultiEmail.tsx. This creates a circular dependency. The import 'import { Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip } from "@calcom/ui"' in MultiEmail.tsx should use relative imports instead to avoid this circular reference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:35 — The handler eagerly loads booking.user credentials but then re-fetches organizer data and separately loads ctx.user credentials, leaving dead data and multiple user sources to keep straight

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }` in the booking query (lines 38-43), but then separately fetches organizer data with a different query (lines 56-66) and uses `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (line 159) instead of the already-loaded booking.user.credentials. This creates redundant data fetching and potential confusion about which user's credentials should be used. While not a bug per se (the code likely works), it's a legitimate code quality/architecture concern that could lead to maintenance issues or subtle bugs if the wrong credentials source is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The unbounded guests array lets one request create arbitrarily many attendees and trigger proportional calendar and email work, enabling severe resource exhaustion.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZAddGuestsInputSchema at line 5 defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no maximum length constraint. The addGuests.handler.ts processes each guest by creating database records, updating calendar attendees via eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(), and sending emails via sendAddGuestsEmails(). A malicious user could submit thousands of email addresses in a single request, causing proportional database writes, calendar API calls, and email sends - a clear resource exhaustion vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:75 — Duplicate filtering scans every existing attendee and blacklist entry for every guest, making large additions quadratic instead of using lookup sets.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at line 75 uses Array.some() inside a filter(), which is O(n*m) complexity where n is the number of guests and m is the number of existing attendees + blacklist entries. While this is technically correct code that will work, it could be optimized using Set lookups for O(n) complexity. However, this is a performance optimization concern rather than a bug - the code will function correctly. For typical booking scenarios with small numbers of guests and attendees, this is unlikely to cause real issues, but it's a valid architectural concern for the new code being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:540 — Each attendee performs a linear newGuests lookup, making notification classification quadratic for large guest additions.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a quadratic complexity issue at line 540, but looking at the actual code in the diff (lines 522-545), the newGuests.includes() check is O(n) where n is the number of new guests, and this is done for each attendee. For typical use cases with small numbers of guests (usually < 10), this is negligible. The 'quadratic' characterization is technically accurate but practically irrelevant - this is not a real performance concern for any realistic guest list size. This is a premature optimization concern, not a real defect or important issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — Promise.all launches every organizer, team-member, and attendee email concurrently with no batching or concurrency limit, causing resource spikes on large bookings.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that sendAddGuestsEmails (lines 522-550) uses Promise.all to send emails to organizer, team members, and all attendees concurrently without any batching or concurrency limit. This is a real pattern in the diff at line 549. However, this is not a bug per se - it's a scalability/architecture concern. The same pattern exists in other email functions in this file (like sendLocationChangeEmails), so this is consistent with existing code patterns. For typical bookings with a handful of attendees, this works fine. It becomes a concern only for unusually large bookings. This is a legitimate non-bug concern about resource usage at scale, grounded in the actual diff code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — Attendees are committed before calendar synchronization, so a calendar failure leaves a partial update that a retry rejects as already added.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the code at lines 82-99 first updates the database with `prisma.booking.update` to add attendees, then later at line 156 calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` to sync with the calendar. If the calendar update fails, the attendees are already committed to the database. On retry, the `uniqueGuests` filter at lines 68-72 would filter out the already-added guests (since they're now in booking.attendees), potentially resulting in an empty list and throwing 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error. This is a real atomicity/consistency bug where partial state can occur.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Incoming duplicate addresses are not deduplicated server-side, so concurrent or non-UI callers can create duplicate attendee records or trigger a database failure.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, the `uniqueGuests` filter on line 74 only checks against existing `booking.attendees` to remove duplicates that are already in the database. However, if the `guests` array itself contains duplicate email addresses (e.g., ['a@b.com', 'a@b.com']), these are not deduplicated before being passed to `createMany`. The client-side validation in AddGuestsDialog.tsx uses a Zod schema with a uniqueness check, but this is only enforced on the UI. Direct API callers or concurrent requests could bypass this and create duplicate attendee records in the database.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Email delivery failures are swallowed after the mutation succeeds, so bookings can be updated without notifications and no retry is scheduled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff at lines 167-171 shows a try-catch block that catches email sending errors and only logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' without rethrowing or implementing any retry mechanism. The mutation has already succeeded at this point (database updated, calendar updated), so guests are added but notifications may silently fail. This is a real concern about silent failure handling, but it's not strictly a bug since the core functionality (adding guests) works - it's more of a reliability/observability concern that a reviewer might flag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Authorizing any attendee lets an attendee add arbitrary outsiders and disclose private meeting links, passwords, and participant details to them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that authorization at line 52 checks `isAttendee` which allows any attendee of a booking to add guests. Looking at the code, an attendee can call `addGuestsHandler`, pass the authorization check (since `isAttendee` is true for them), and then add arbitrary email addresses as guests. These new guests receive emails with meeting details including video call URLs and passwords (via `sendAddGuestsEmails` and the `evt` object containing `videoCallData`). This is a security vulnerability where an attendee can disclose private meeting information to unauthorized third parties.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Guest addresses are not normalized before comparison with the lowercase blacklist, so changing email case bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in addGuests.handler.ts lines 68-77, the blacklist is created with lowercase emails: `.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`. However, in the filter on line 73-76, the guest emails are compared directly without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not lowercased before comparison, a user could bypass the blacklist by using different casing (e.g., 'BLOCKED@example.com' would not match 'blocked@example.com' in the blacklist).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The guest array has no size or uniqueness limit, allowing one permitted request to trigger unbounded database writes and email/calendar fan-out.

adjudication.rationale: The schema in addGuests.schema.ts defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no maximum length constraint. Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, each guest triggers: 1) database writes via `prisma.booking.update` with `createMany`, 2) calendar updates via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and 3) email sends via `sendAddGuestsEmails`. A malicious user could pass thousands of email addresses in a single request, causing unbounded resource consumption. While there's a uniqueness check against existing attendees, there's no limit on the array size itself, making this a real security/DoS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Missing role-specific authorization coverage leaves admins and owners denied because the two mutually exclusive role checks are combined with &&.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a logic error on line 46. The code uses `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` which requires the user to be BOTH admin AND owner simultaneously. This is likely incorrect - it should probably be `||` (OR) to allow either admins or owners. As written, this would deny access to users who are only admins or only owners, which contradicts the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. This is a real authorization bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Missing case-variant coverage lets uppercase forms of blacklisted addresses bypass filtering because only blacklist entries are lowercased.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in addGuests.handler.ts lines 68-75, the blacklist filtering code lowercases the blacklist entries but does not lowercase the guest emails being compared. The code is: `blacklistedGuestEmails.split(',').map((email) => email.toLowerCase())` for the blacklist, but then compares with `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is not lowercased. This means if a blacklisted email is 'bad@example.com' and a user submits 'BAD@example.com', it would bypass the filter. This is a real correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Missing API-level duplicate coverage lets repeated guest addresses reach createMany because uniqueGuests never deduplicates the request.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts lines 68-74, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails that already exist in `booking.attendees`, but it does NOT deduplicate the input `guests` array itself. If a user submits `guests: ['a@b.com', 'a@b.com']`, both would pass the filter (since neither is in existing attendees yet) and both would be passed to `createMany`. While the frontend has a Zod schema with a uniqueness check, the API-level handler lacks this deduplication, which is a defense-in-depth issue that could cause duplicate attendee records.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Missing mixed existing-and-new guest coverage misclassifies requested existing attendees as new because email dispatch receives guests instead of uniqueGuests.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 168 in addGuests.handler.ts: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` - the function passes `guests` (the original input array) instead of `uniqueGuests` (the filtered array that excludes existing attendees). This means if someone tries to add a mix of new and existing emails, the email logic in sendAddGuestsEmails will receive the full list including existing attendees. Looking at email-manager.ts lines 536-541, the code checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide whether to send AttendeeScheduledEmail (for new guests) or AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (for existing attendees). If `guests` contains emails of existing attendees, they would incorrectly receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. This is a real bug where the wrong parameter is passed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:32 — Missing initial-state coverage leaves the dialog starting with an invalid empty-string email instead of the MultiEmail empty state.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a bug with 'missing initial-state coverage' leaving the dialog with an 'invalid empty-string email'. Looking at the diff, line 32 shows `const [multiEmailValue, setMultiEmailValue] = useState<string[]>(['']);`. This is intentional design - the MultiEmail component (also in the diff) handles arrays of strings and shows input fields for each element. Starting with [''] gives users one empty input field to type into. The handleAdd function at line 48-56 validates emails before submission using ZAddGuestsInputSchema, and the validation would catch empty strings. This is not a bug - it's the expected UX pattern for this type of multi-input component.
